Adriano Battista Doctoral researcher, teacher, published author, and education & policy advocate.

Research profile

Academic researcher + public educator.

Adriano Battista is a doctoral researcher, educator, and published author specializing in youth homelessness prevention, upstream prevention, teacher education, education policy, and school-based early intervention systems. His research explores how schools can function as prevention spaces by helping educators recognize and respond to poverty, trauma, housing instability, and social vulnerability before youth homelessness becomes visible as crisis.

His work brings together education policy, critical pedagogy, lived and professional experience, and prevention-focused school systems, including the Community of Schools and Services model and upstream prevention approaches. Adriano is also involved in Quebec prevention work through Les Visages de la Prévention and emerging school-community initiatives focused on youth homelessness awareness, prevention education, and training for school staff.

In plain sight

The data points toward schools, care systems, and early intervention.

These figures are presented as decision-support signals. Each statistic links back to a cited source so readers can examine the evidence directly.

20%

of emergency-shelter users in Canada are youth aged 13 to 24. (ESDC, 2017)

40,000+

young people are estimated to be experiencing homelessness in Canada over the course of this year. (Homeless Hub, n.d.)

46%

Nearly half of chronically homeless adults first experienced homelessness before turning 25. (Homeless Hub, 2025)

1 in 3

More than one-third of youth placed by child protection services experienced homelessness in the first years following placement. (Goyette et al., 2024)
